Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates extensive bilateral consolidation with distinct cystic lucencies (pneumatoceles) in the right midzone, a pattern highly characteristic of severe necrotizing bacterial pneumonia (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus or Klebsiella). While adenocarcinoma can present similarly, the acute appearance and specific morphology of the lucencies favor an infectious etiology over malignancy or other chronic processes.
